newsitem.title: SIERRA LEONE: Britain to evacuate Westerners from Sierra Leone.
newsitem.headline: Britain to evacuate Westerners from Sierra Leone.

text.p: Britain plans to begin evacuating its citizens and other Westeners from Sierra Leone on Thursday as regional power Nigeria builds up a military force to challenge coup leaders in the West African nation.
Helicopters would start ferrying evacuees from Freetown during the morning and take them across a vast river estuary to the capital's Lungi international airport, British diplomats said.
A chartered jumbo jet was due to land around midday (1200 GMT) and could carry as many as 500 people, including Britons, Canadians, Australians and Danes, said the diplomats.

Embassy staff say there are several hundred European Union citizens in Sierra Leone. Some 40 Americans are attached to the U.S. embassy in Freetown and there are about 400 other Americans in Sierra Leone, mostly aid workers and missionaries, according to U.S. officials.

The evacuation of foreigners staying in a few overcrowded hotels in the steamy, seaside capital has taken on added urgency because of moves by Nigeria to reverse Sunday's military coup, which has been condemned internationally.
"We are praying that the Nigerians don't move in the middle of the evacuation," said a British diplomat.
West African military sources acknowledged that a steady buildup of Nigerian troops was part of a regional plan to reinstate elected President Ahmad Tejan Kabbah, who escaped by helicopter to Guinea.
No military move was expected until the evacuations were completed, the sources said.
"I think that is one of the things holding up a quick strike against the coup leaders," said one source.
A Nigerian Air Force Hercules C-130 plane flew two missions from neighbouring Liberia on Wednesday to land combat troops and supplies at Lungi.

Three Nigerian frigates docked in Freetown with troops on Tuesday to bolster the West African ECOMOG peacekeeping contingent that was based in Sierra Leone when low-ranking soldiers seized power on Sunday.
Nigeria's military ruler General Sani Abacha has been denounced in the West for his faltering plan to end army rule in his own country and his government's human rights record.

But he has won reluctant credit for pressing on with a costly regional peacekeeping mission in Liberia which has a mandate that extends to helping the Sierra Leone government in a fight against rebels.

Despite Washington's strong disapproval of Abacha's government, U.S. State Department spokesman John Dinger said the Nigerians had been playing a "useful role" in Sierra Leone as leader of the ECOMOG force.
Nigeria is the backbone of the Economic Community of West Africa Monitoring Group (ECOMOG) which was first sent to Liberia in 1990.
A Boeing 707 plane sent by Lebanon evacuated 178 Lebanese, most of them women and children, on Wednesday, witnesses said.
The bodies of two Lebanese men killed in the coup were loaded on to the Middle East Airlines plane.
Lebanese dominate the retail trade and other businesses in Sierra Leone and have suffered huge losses from looting by rampaging soldiers.
The soldiers have also targeted private homes and United Nations offices and housing compounds.
The United States said on Wednesday it was cutting the number of American personnel at its embassy in Freetown and making plans for an emergency evacuation if needed.
"The Department of State has ordered a drawdown of United States embassy non-essential personnel and dependants," Dinger told reporters in Washington.
"Contingency plans for an emergency evacuation, should that prove necessary, are also being developed," he added.
Dinger said the U.S. Navy helicopter ship Kearsarge had been ordered to head towards Sierra Leone and would be in place shortly.
The United States, the United Nations, the Organisation of African Unity and several governments have condemned the coup led by Major Johnny Paul Koromah.
Dinger called on Koromah's new Armed Forces Revolutionary Council to return power immediately to the elected government.

"The leaders of this coup need to understand that if they wish international support, if they wish for a true future of stability and prosperity for Sierra Leone, they have to reverse their action," he said.
Koromah has banned political activity and suspended the constitution.
His council banned a demonstration called by civilian opponents of the coup for Wednesday to demand the return of Kabbah, whose government was elected in March 1996 after four years of military rule.
